name: ybug
description: Read, filter and triage Ybug website feedback and bug reports, including screenshots, console logs and network requests.

interface.longDescription:
Ybug collects visual feedback and bug reports from your website: a screenshot, the page URL, browser, device, screen size, and optionally console logs and network requests. Connect Ybug to ChatGPT and read those reports here, so you don’t copy them into chat by hand.

Ask what came in on a project this week and get it grouped by page. Ask why a report happened, and ChatGPT reads the page, browser, console errors and failed requests before suggesting the likely cause. Or work through new feedback: ChatGPT suggests priorities, types, tags and assignees, and applies the ones you approve with an internal note.

What it can do:
- Find feedback by status, priority, type, tags, assignee, date or keyword
- Read a report in full, including screenshot and video links, console logs and network requests
- Read a report’s comments and the team’s tags and members
- Change status, priority, type, assignee and tags, create tags, and add internal comments

Limitations: it can’t delete anything, change settings or send public replies to reporters. Comments it adds are always internal. Moving a report to a Resolved or Closed status can send the reporter your auto-reply, if you’ve turned it on.

You sign in to Ybug, pick a team and approve access. ChatGPT acts as you and sees only the projects you can access. Reporter email addresses, phone numbers and the user data your site passes to the widget are never sent. You can revoke access any time under Connected apps in your Ybug account.

Requires a Ybug account. Which actions are available depends on your Ybug plan and your permissions in the team.
capabilities: Read bug reports with console logs and network requests
Read comments, tags and project members
Update status, priority, type, assignee and tags
Add internal comments and create tags
defaultPrompt: What feedback came in on my Ybug project this week? Group it by page.
Show me open high-priority bugs in Ybug that nobody is assigned to.
Read my newest Ybug bug report and explain the likely cause.

positive.description: Summarize a project’s feedback by priority
positive.prompt: In Ybug, summarize all feedback in Demo project and sort it by priority.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Demo project, lists its five reports and sorts them by priority: the cookie banner hiding Place order (Highest) first, then the rejected SPRING10 coupon (High), then the rest. Each item shows its title, status and report id.

positive.prompt: In Ybug, which reports in Demo project have High or Highest priority?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the project’s priority names with get_project, then calls list_feedback with the priorities filter. Returns the cookie banner report (Highest) and the SPRING10 coupon report (High), and nothing else.

positive.description: Investigate a bug from its console logs
positive.prompt: In Ybug, why does the SPRING10 coupon fail in Demo project? Check the console logs.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the coupon report with a keyword search, reads it with get_feedback, then reads its two console errors with get_feedback_console_logs. Explains the likely cause using the page, browser and the error messages, without inventing details that aren’t in the report.

positive.prompt: In Ybug, what does the team say in the comments on the SPRING10 coupon report in Demo project?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the coupon report and calls list_comments with its id. Summarizes the internal comment and names its author. No email addresses appear.

positive.description: Add an internal note after confirmation
positive.prompt: In Ybug, add an internal note to the GBP currency report in Demo project saying “Looking into this today.”
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the currency report and calls add_comment. Confirms the note was added as an internal comment that the reporter doesn’t see. The note appears on the report in the Ybug dashboard.

negative.description: Deletion isn’t supported. There is no delete tool, so ChatGPT should say it can’t delete feedback and not change anything else instead.
negative.prompt: In Ybug, delete all feedback in Demo project.

negative.description: Public replies to reporters aren’t supported. Comments added through the plugin are always internal, so ChatGPT should explain that it can’t reply to the reporter and offer an internal note instead, not present an internal note as a reply.
negative.prompt: In Ybug, reply to the person who reported the “Get in tuch” typo and tell them it’s fixed.

negative.description: Reporter contact details are never returned. ChatGPT should say the email address isn’t available through Ybug rather than guess one.
negative.prompt: In Ybug, what’s the email address of the person who reported the cookie banner bug in Demo project?

review.commerce_description: This plugin doesn’t sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: read, filter and triage Ybug feedback, including console logs and network requests.
